# A -> B transfer: A_to_B

**Real data.** Generated by `bre.realdata`; no hand-typed numbers.

Protocol: Fit the population parts of B1, B3 and Q2 on the choices13k aggregate choice rates (one pseudo-subject, encoder random effect u frozen at 0, binomial weights = respondents per rate, contexts = feedback/block tags, loss magnitude = |min(0, worst outcome / max |outcome|)| of the problem, response = share choosing gamble B); score the fitted parameters without refitting on the CPC15 rates and on the CPC18 per-problem B-rates computed from the individual rows (per problem x block); compare with the same model refitted on the target's training problems and with a constant rate, all on the target's held-out 20% of problems; metrics: weighted NLL per respondent, Brier score, Pearson and Spearman correlation of predicted vs observed rates, problem-level bootstrap 95% intervals.

Source A: choices13k (catalog A), 12225 rate rows, 204501 respondent-choices; contexts ['news:recession', 'news:technical', 'social:friend_sells', 'market:recovered_5pct', 'block:1', 'block:2', 'block:3', 'block:4', 'block:5', 'feedback:off', 'feedback:on']; loss_pct = min(0, x_worst_outcome_rel); response = share choosing gamble B.
Target cpc15: cpc15 (catalog B), 750 rate rows over 150 problems; held-out 30 problems (150 rows); weights: not in the mirror: every rate weighs 1.
Target cpc18_agg: cpc18 (per-problem B-rates from the individual rows) (catalog B), 1050 rate rows over 210 problems; held-out 42 problems (210 rows); weights: respondents per rate.
Fit settings: restarts 5, steps 1500, lr 0.02, L-BFGS polish 100 it, seed 0; bootstrap over problems.

## Fits on A

| model | n_params (population) | train NLL/row | val NLL/row | best restart | seconds |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| B1 | 203 | 11.6085 | 11.5542 | 3 | 18 |
| B3 | 97 | 11.6102 | 11.5536 | 4 | 40 |
| Q2 | 129 | 11.6005 | 11.5539 | 2 | 184 |

Reading: a transferred fit that scores no better than the constant rate on a target carries no information across datasets; a refit that beats the transfer shows how much of the gap is population shift rather than model form. The response is the share choosing gamble B (CPC convention), so these fits do not speak to the safe-choice analog of the Phase 4 evaluation; the population parameters are provenance for the demo mode only when the transfer beats the constant on the held-out problems.
